A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same RD3 study with complete main text and appendices. Tables, figures and the random-sampling analysis relocated from v1 Appendix H to v2 Section 5 can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original reevaluations across six image datasets, computational-efficiency measurements, cross-architecture experiments and numerous ablations, including random-sampling comparisons in Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the multi-dataset evaluations and ablations. The random-sampling results now appear in main-text Table 7.

M1.justification: The RD3 framework, soft-label evaluation procedure and investigated initialization and loss variants are unchanged. The promoted random-sampling discussion describes an experiment already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, ImageNette, ImageWoof and ImageNet-1K. No dataset, domain or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The eight distillation comparators and supplementary soft-label enhancement comparisons are unchanged. Random sampling in v2 Table 7 was already evaluated in v1 Table 15.

E3.justification: Appendix C retains the same 400-epoch protocol, learning rate, batch-size rules, scheduler factors and augmentations. Architecture configurations and settings for the supplementary experiments are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Initialization, hybrid-label, loss, temperature, augmentation and generalization analyses are retained, together with training-dynamics and t-SNE analyses. Moving the random-sampling analysis into the main text introduces no additional test.

E5.justification: The same uncertainty-reporting practice and ± entries are retained. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and graphical evidence are unchanged. For example, v1 Table 15 and v2 Table 7 both report ImageNet-1K random-sampling soft-label accuracy of 61.8 ± 0.2 at IPC=50 and 64.1 ± 0.2 at IPC=100.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, the dataset-distillation formulations and the learning-rate scheduler formula are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about standardized evaluation, confounding from evaluation settings and the importance of efficiency and generalization. The foregrounded random-sampling finding already appeared in v1.

C2.justification: The closing paragraph of v1 Appendix H identifies balancing diversity and representativeness and preserving hard-label discriminability as research priorities. Its replacement in v2 Section 5 explicitly recommends adopting random sampling with soft labels as a comparative benchmark. The underlying mechanisms and dataset-dependent interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit RD3 code-repository link to the abstract, providing access information absent from v1. Implementation details and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive comparisons with earlier research, including DC-Bench, PCA and DD-Ranking, are unchanged. The Xiao et al. citation accompanying the random-sampling analysis moves with that discussion.

P1.justification: v1 Appendix H becomes v2 Section 5 with a new heading and closing paragraph; the conclusion and subsequent appendices are renumbered. v2 also adds an acknowledgement and conference-publication headers. Most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The random-sampling table moves from appendix Table 15 to main-text Table 7, and other displays are repositioned without changing their content. A new layout defect on v2 page 8 causes Table 3's caption to overlap parts of the headers of Tables 4 and 5.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility documentation through its code-access link and makes the existing random-sampling baseline finding and recommendation more prominent. These modest gains are tempered by the localized table-caption overlap on page 8. The scientific evidence and principal claims remain unchanged.
